An ultrabook, in general terms, refers to a laptop that combines the best characteristics of both tablets and desktops, giving you a versatile and powerful device that’s perfect for work and play. It’s typically slim and lightweight (hence the ‘ultra’ in the name), and features an 11.6-inch or 13.3-inch (or larger) display, often with a fast processor, high-resolution screen, low power consumption and long battery life.
The ultra-lightweight ultrabook has become a popular category for those looking for something in between a small and lightweight tablet and a traditional desktop computer. The term “ultra lightweight” is used to describe laptops that weigh less than 2.2 pounds (1kg), while the term “ultra slim” is used to describe laptops that have a screen size of 13.3 inches (or larger). They are designed to be very flexible and portable and allow you to accomplish your work, regardless of where you are.
In addition to their ultra-lightweight qualities, laptops in the Ultrabook category also offer some essential features:
They come in both 13.3 inches and 11.6 inches in screen size formats.
The battery life of most Ultrabooks is between 11-18 hours.
Most Ultrabooks feature Intel or AMD processors with up to 2.9GHz clock speeds or more.
The Ultrabook category offers laptops with touchscreens and those with an external keyboard in select models.
Some Ultrabooks feature a touchpad or trackpad on the right side instead of the center of the display screen like you’d expect from an actual smartphone. Alternatively, you can also find laptops with a full laptop keyboard built into the device where a touchpad would normally be.
